intro.title: Race Condition Fix
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a simple Angular application that fetches and displays a list of users from a mock API. You will learn how to fix a race condition, a common bug where the order of asynchronous operations can cause unpredictable results. Using Angular's HttpClient and RxJS operators like switchMap, you will ensure that only the latest API request is processed. This beginner-friendly project will help you understand how to manage asynchronous data flows safely in real-world applications.
intro.usecase: Race conditions frequently occur in Angular applications when multiple asynchronous operations compete for shared resources, such as data fetching in dashboards with real-time updates. For example, when users rapidly change filters on an analytics dashboard, multiple HTTP requests may be sent, and later responses can overwrite newer data, displaying incorrect metrics. Similarly, in e-commerce product listings, clicking different category filters in quick succession can cause the wrong products to appear. Developers must implement cancellation patterns or state tracking to ensure only the most relevant data updates the UI, preventing confusing user experiences.
